newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar ends weaker on sliding bonds.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar ends weaker on sliding bonds.

text.p: * Canada's dollar ended weaker on Wednesday at C$1.3817 (US$0.7237) from Tuesday's close of C$1.3780 (US$0.7256) under pressure from weaker Canadian bonds, dealers said.
* They said the Canadian dollar eased in mid-afternoon trading following a poor reception for 10-year Government of Canada bonds.
Analysts said the Canada dollar would likely slide overnight as investors refocused on a possible U.S. Federal Reserve interest rate hike at the next FOMC meeting on May 20.
"Given current interest spreads, Canada will come under pressure going into the FOMC," one trader said.
Others feared that the Bre-X Minerals Ltd scandal could turn foreign investors off Canadian stocks and trigger a further sell-off of the currency.
Major international newspapers ran stories this week critical of Canada's stock markets.
